question: A post blamed smartphones for American obesity, with this chart: two lines rising in perfect step. Where's the trick?
answer: In the two scales, each stretched until the lines matched. On one axis, phone owners rose 42 points and obesity 7. Obesity had already climbed from about 23% to 31% of adults in the 1990s, before any smartphone. Anything that grew in the 2010s tracks anything else that grew: a shared calendar, not a cause.
move: When two rising lines match, ask what else rose over those years.
ask: What do I blame on something new that was already happening before it arrived?

scene.headline: Smartphones are making America fat
scene.label: US adults, %
scene.found: Yes: each line has its own scale, set to make them match.
scene.miss: That part is fair. Compare the numbers on the two sides of the chart.

misses.marks: Both lines are real survey figures. It's how they were lined up that persuades.
misses.headline: That's the claim. The drawing is what makes it look proven.

scene.name: Two axes, one story
scene.lesson: Two scales can make any two rising lines move as one. Put them on one axis first.

source: CDC NHANES obesity data; Pew smartphone surveys
